title_candidates: Turn an AI-made boundary file into a checked map
Map public boundaries with AI - then verify the outline
summary: A new browser tool turns GeoJSON from ChatGPT Work into a styled map and PNG. The useful habit is checking every AI-made boundary against an official source.

primary_source.title: Tool: GeoJSON Map Viewer
primary_source.author: Simon Willison
key_facts: Simon Willison needed a quick way to display local political-boundary GeoJSON files on a map and export the result as a PNG.
After he asked GPT-5.6-Sol to suggest existing tools, the model instead built a viewer that he refined with Claude Code for web and Fable 5.1.
Willison also used ChatGPT Work to assemble boundary polygons from public government data in response to plain-language requests.
The finished browser viewer accepts pasted GeoJSON or loads it from a compatible public URL.
Users can overlay multiple shapes, change each fill colour and opacity, and arrange which shape appears on top.
The viewer exports the current map view as a PNG with selectable dimensions and resolution.
The page says pasted GeoJSON stays in the browser, while shared page URLs can encode source URLs, styling, map position, and export settings.
An AI-generated boundary still needs comparison with an authoritative map or data layer before anyone relies on or shares it.

quote_candidates.text: I asked GPT-5.6-Sol for suggestions of tools and it proactively built one.
Your GeoJSON stays in this browser.

supporting_sources.title: GeoJSON Map Viewer
key_facts: The live tool accepts GeoJSON Geometry, Feature, and FeatureCollection data, supports multiple styled overlays, and can export a PNG.
Its interface says pasted GeoJSON stays in the browser.

supporting_sources.title: Using cloud browser in ChatGPT
key_facts: OpenAI says ChatGPT Work's cloud browser is available on paid ChatGPT plans in supported regions, subject to rollout and workspace permissions.
OpenAI tells users to check a completed task and its sources before relying on the result.

supporting_sources.title: Granada Community Services District
key_facts: San Mateo County LAFCo publishes an official district profile and map for the Granada Community Services District.
The county page identifies the communities served, giving readers concrete landmarks for an independent map check.

prerequisites: A paid ChatGPT plan with ChatGPT Work available
A modern desktop browser and permission to download a GeoJSON file and PNG
Only public sample data - no private addresses, customer locations, or confidential files

steps.instruction: Start a new ChatGPT Work task and ask it to create a GeoJSON FeatureCollection for the exact Granada Community Services District boundary near Half Moon Bay, using only official government sources, WGS84 longitude-latitude coordinates, source URLs, and a retrieval date; tell it not to request private address data. Download the result as granada-gcsd.geojson, and stop if Work cannot cite an official source or produce valid GeoJSON.

Open the file in a text editor. Confirm it begins with a GeoJSON object such as FeatureCollection and that the coordinates are near longitude -122 and latitude 37; compare its structure with Willison's public Granada example, then stop if the coordinates point elsewhere, include personal information, or cannot be traced to a source.

Open the GeoJSON Map Viewer, paste the file into Shape 1, choose a fill colour and about 50% opacity, and click Render map; check that a shaded coastal district appears around the communities named on the official county page.

Compare the rendered coastline and district edges with San Mateo County LAFCo's official Granada Community Services District map. Stop and do not publish or rely on the AI-made boundary if the outlines materially disagree; instead ask Work to regenerate from the cited government layer.
After the boundary matches, adjust the map position, PNG size, and resolution, click Export PNG, inspect the preview for clipped edges or unreadable labels, and click Download PNG.

risk_flags: ChatGPT Work availability depends on a paid plan, supported region, rollout, and workspace permissions.
The article treats AI-generated boundary data as a draft and requires comparison with the county's official map before use.
The guide uses a public district example and explicitly excludes private addresses, customer locations, and confidential data.
The viewer keeps pasted GeoJSON in the browser, but public source URLs and shareable page URLs can still expose information a user places in them.
